Finding 1 tightens parseJsonBody in lib/realtor-api.ts (or adds caller-side guards in profile/page.tsx) — pure TS, verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck` + `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web test`. evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/realtor-api.ts:68-79 — parseJsonBody<T> was added (ref #2276/#2281/#2341) to stop a malformed 200 from crashing 'deep in a component' (its own doc comment, L58-59, cites `res.listings.map`). But the guard only enforces 'non-null, non-array object' (L75); it does NOT validate that the expected array/scalar fields are present. A 200 whose body is a valid object missing the contract field (e.g. `{}`, or `{listings: null}`, or `{total: 0}` without `reviews`) passes the guard and is returned typed as T — so the exact crash the fix targets is still reachable.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:137 — `listMyListings().then((res) => setListings(res.listings))`: if `res.listings` is absent, `listings` state becomes `undefined`. Rendering then hits ListingsTab L445 `if (listings.length === 0)` → `undefined.length` throws (React error boundary / white panel). The `.catch` at L139 does NOT cover this: the deref `res.listings` returns undefined without throwing, so the failure moves to render time, exactly the 'throws deep in a component' symptom the boundary guard was meant to prevent.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:160-161 `setReviews(res)` from getRealtorReviews, then ReviewsTab L548 `if (!reviews || reviews.reviews.length === 0)` — the guard checks `reviews` truthiness but not `reviews.reviews`; a `{}` 200 body makes `reviews.reviews.length` throw. L191 `reviews.total` and L195 `reviews.avg_rating.toFixed(1)` have the same exposure.

Severity MEDIUM (+2): reachable render crash on an authenticated user-facing page (profile) whenever the server/proxy emits a partial-but-object 200 — the scenario the parseJsonBody fix explicitly set out to close, left half-open. Confidence medium: the throw is statically certain given a field-missing object body; the likelihood of such a 200 under the real reality-server contract is the uncertain part (static-only, no runtime confirmation). Fix: make parseJsonBody accept a lightweight shape predicate (or add per-endpoint `Array.isArray(body.listings)` / `Array.isArray(body.reviews)` checks) so array fields are validated at the boundary, and/or default to `res.listings ?? []` / `res.reviews ?? []` at the call sites in profile/page.tsx.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/realtor-api.ts:35,73,76,38 — RealtorApiError is thrown with hardcoded English messages ('Network error. Please try again.', 'Malformed response from server.', `Request failed (${status})`). These are not log-only: the realtor/account CRUD pages surface `err.message` verbatim to the user.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/profile/page.tsx:48,82 — `setLoadError(err instanceof RealtorApiError ? err.message : 'Could not load profile.')` and `setSaveError(... : 'Could not save profile.')`: BOTH branches are English on a 6-locale portal (sk/cs/de/en/pl/hu) — the RealtorApiError branch shows the untranslated lib string, the fallback branch a hardcoded English literal. Same pattern at realtor/listings/new/page.tsx:27 ('Could not create listing. Please try again.'), realtor/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx:42,61 ('Could not load listing.' / 'Could not save listing.'), realtor/analytics/page.tsx:54 ('Could not load analytics.').

This is the skill Frontend pattern 'hardcoded user-facing string that should be in i18n', on error/empty paths across the realtor-portal CRUD surface. Distinct from the done/prior reality-web i18n rows (ComparisonView, RealtorManagement, AgencyErrorStates, the 2026-10-25 analytics-page body copy and inquiry-enum) — this cluster is specifically the thrown-error message strings in realtor-api.ts plus the error-state fallbacks in the realtor/* and account/* pages. Note account/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx:166,213 use Slovak literals ('Načítanie inzerátu zlyhalo.' / 'Uloženie zlyhalo, skúste znova.'), i.e. hardcoded the OTHER direction — same i18n-bypass class, confirming the error strings route around next-intl entirely.

Severity LOW (+1): no crash; localization gap on error surfaces only. Confidence medium: the hardcoded strings are statically certain; impact depends on how often these error paths fire. Fix: route RealtorApiError messages through an error-code → next-intl key map (or carry a code on the error and translate at the call site), and replace the English/Slovak literal fallbacks with `t('...')` keys in messages/{en,sk,cs,de,pl,hu}.json.
